inputs.description: User objective, constraints and intended deliverable.
Released source evidence, definitions, provenance and known limitations.

name: Research and design
goal: Investigate the supplied evidence and propose a defensible new design direction or conclude that evidence is insufficient.

workers.name: Lead investigator
workers.instructions: Separate observed facts from interpretations and preserve dissent.
workers.task: Organize the evidence and synthesize the final recommendation.

workers.name: Falsifier
workers.instructions: Find testable alternative explanations and decisive defects, without requiring impossible certainty.
workers.task: Challenge measurement, causal claims and proposed mechanisms.

workers.name: Designer A
workers.instructions: Develop mechanisms from evidence rather than familiar defaults.
workers.task: Form an independent diagnosis, then propose distinct design concepts.

workers.name: Designer B
workers.instructions: Consider competing mechanisms independently and make uncertainty explicit.
workers.task: Form an independent diagnosis and alternative design concepts.

stages.instruction: Explain what the evidence establishes, competing explanations, contradictions and falsifiers. Do not design a replacement yet.
Compare diagnoses and derive supported requirements. Name missing decisive measurements; do not claim they have been performed.
Independently propose up to two materially different concepts with mechanisms, observables, failure cases and minimal falsification experiments. Do not inspect peer drafts.
Critique every concept fairly. Architects focus on the other architect's cards. Identify strongest cases, material objections and distinguishing tests.
Make one documented response/revision. Do not claim proposed experiments were executed or create an untested compromise.
Recommend a bounded next direction, at most one reserve with a distinguishing test, or no recommendation. Preserve dissent and distinguish plausibility from validation.
